Block settings are not applied to crew entries.

terms.meaning: a team a fan picks from real players for one match, scored by how those players perform

sections.name: File setup, MatchRow, TeamRow, toMatch, toTeam
sections.title: Imports and display shapes
sections.what: Brings in the rules check, the membership checks and the database calls. Also converts stored matches and teams into browser shapes, turning dates into text.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps raw database objects away from the browser.

sections.name: openMatchesForCrew
sections.title: Open matches for a crew
sections.what: Lists the matches still open for picking, upcoming or in progress, for a member of the crew.
sections.why: Likely reason: the membership check stops outsiders seeing match lists tied to a crew.

sections.name: getContest
sections.title: One match in a crew
sections.what: Returns a match with the signed-in fan's own team and the crew size. A non-member gets a not-found error.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the match page show whether the fan has already picked a team.

sections.name: contestEntries
sections.title: Crew teams for a match
sections.what: Returns every crew member's team for one match with their public details, sorted by points.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a crew compare teams, limited to crew members.
sections.watch_out: Blocked members' teams and names are not hidden here, unlike on the crew page.

sections.name: crewStandings
sections.title: Crew standings
sections.what: Adds up each member's points from finished matches and lists them highest first, with name order as the tie breaker.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared scoreboard for the crew.
sections.watch_out: Only finished matches count, so points for live matches do not show until they finish.

sections.name: builderPlayers
sections.title: Players for the team builder
sections.what: Gets the match and then lists players from both sides with their playing status and stats, in the shape the builder needs.
sections.why: Likely reason: the builder needs its own tidy shape rather than raw database rows.
sections.watch_out: A missing appearance record shows the player as not playing.

sections.name: submitTeam
sections.title: Submitting a fan's team
sections.what: Checks the match is still open for selection, checks the team against the game rules, saves it, and refuses a second team for the same match with a conflict message.
sections.why: Likely reason: the status check stops picks after play starts, and the database rule backs up the one-team limit even when two requests race.
sections.watch_out: This function does not check crew membership, so any signed-in user who knows a match ID can submit a team. The reason is not stated in the code.

summary: Runs contest actions: listing matches, showing teams, standings, the team builder, and submitting a team.
purpose: Business rules for fantasy-style contests inside crews.
why: Likely reason: membership checks stop people from seeing contest data for crews they are not in.
how: 1. Check crew membership. 2. Find the match. 3. Read teams or players. 4. For submission, check the match is open, check the team against the rules, save it, and turn a duplicate into a conflict message.
inputs: A user ID, crew ID, match ID, and team choices.
outputs: Match details, team lists, standings, builder players, or a new team ID.
risks: submitTeam does not check crew membership. Crew entry lists show blocked members' names.
debug: Not found usually means a wrong ID or no membership. Closed means the match is no longer upcoming. Conflict means a team already exists for that match.
